title: Senate Committee Hearing
subtitle: Senate Judiciary Committee — Gun Violence and Firearms Policy in America

metadata.laymanSummary: The Senate Judiciary Committee heard expert testimony on gun violence statistics, red flag law effectiveness, and competing legislative approaches to reducing firearm deaths.

data.billTitle: Hearing: The State of Gun Violence in America — Data, Policy, and Pathways Forward

speakers.name: Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse
speakers.title: D-RI · Senate Judiciary
speakers.quote: The United States has 4.2 firearm deaths per 100,000 people. Canada has 2.1. Australia has 1.0. Germany has 0.9. These countries are not less free than we are. They are not less armed — they are less dead. The difference is policy, not culture. Policy choices are reversible.

speakers.name: Sen. Ted Cruz
speakers.title: R-TX · Senate Judiciary
speakers.quote: Every mass shooting in the past decade — every single one — was carried out by someone who either passed a background check or obtained their weapon illegally. The answer is not to burden 330 million law-abiding Americans. The answer is mental health intervention, school security, and prosecuting existing gun laws that go unenforced.

speakers.name: Sen. Rand Paul
speakers.title: R-KY · Senate
speakers.quote: 63% of gun deaths in America are suicides. If we actually cared about saving lives instead of political posturing, we would be talking about mental health funding and crisis hotlines — not making it harder for law-abiding people to protect their families. The data doesn't support the legislation being pushed here.

data.title: About This Hearing
data.text: The Senate Judiciary Committee held this hearing on May 11, 2026 ahead of expected votes on both background check legislation and the school safety bill. Witnesses included a CDC epidemiologist, a survivor of the Uvalde shooting, a constitutional law scholar, and the executive director of Gun Owners of America. The hearing lasted six hours and produced no consensus but built the legislative record for subsequent floor votes.
